correctness.rationale: For any m,n≥3 and t,κ>0 the finite-dimensional loss operator has bright subspace span{L^j|w>}. Its explicitly derived five-class quotient has Krylov determinant −m t^3(m−n), hence full rank five iff m≠n. At m=n four successive powers are independent and the displayed dark vector has Laplacian eigenvalue m and zero trap amplitude, yielding rank four and the explicit rank-one projector subtraction. Taking projector diagonal entries proves every claimed capture formula. An independently implemented full-graph exact rational Krylov checker passed all 100 combinations m,n in 3..7 and t in {1/3,1,2,7/2}. Computation is finite corroboration, not the infinite proof. Positivity of t and κ, and the Laplacian rather than adjacency Hamiltonian, are essential boundaries.

originality.rationale: The spectral Krylov method is known (Novo et al., 2014) and the equal-size, unit-bridge four-dimensional barbell case is known (Razzoli et al., 2021), both explicitly credited. In inspected primary full text, no theorem asserts the all-size unequal-clique five-dimensional bright subspace, full bridge capture, and positive-weight rank transition. The related weighted barbell quantum search work (Duda and Wong, 2024) is unitary oracle search, not loss. Results and indexed literature searched by statements and reductions showed no coverage. Priority remains provisional, with possibility of uncatalogued equivalent exact calculations.
residual_risks: An earlier equivalent result for arbitrary unequal two-clique graphs could be absent from the queried indexes.
A broad theorem for general equitable graph partitions may logically imply the rank condition even without the same terminology.
Positive local absorber asymptotic behavior does not directly give finite-time capture speed, which is not claimed.

value.rationale: Two cliques connected by a unique bridge are a canonical finite transport bottleneck, and complete absorption from a site exactly on that bottleneck is a natural operational invariant. The result proves a sharp symmetry-protected loss-free mode at equal clique sizes that vanishes when one site is added, causing a macroscopic 1/2-to-1 jump in bridge-input capture, independently of positive coupling and loss strength. It provides complete finite-size sitewise projections over an infinite two-parameter family, beyond the known equal-size case; this is neither a renamed algorithm nor an isolated arbitrary numerical sample.
